items.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: We had a band, I was with one of Cannonball Adderley’s first bands, him and Nat, and Junior Mance and Sam Jones and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah, well now the bass player, the bass player is supposed to be able to stand up and not have anybody else play with him and you’re supposed to know where everything is. You know if there’s a tune like “Have You Met Miss Jones,” you’re supposed to see Miss Jones all through that, and know where Miss Jones went, whether you met her or not.
That’s a good way to put that, that’s one of the best profiles I want you to know.

items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The band was what I just named: him and Nat, Sam Jones, Junior Mance, and me. We made an album called Sharpshooters.

ctx.x: [Oscar] Pettiford. Pettiford’s band. He sat in with Pettiford, and Pettiford hired him. After that he played with Pettiford a little bit. He felt his way around. I think he got in touch with John Levy and told him he wanted to have a band. So he got a band and brought some guys from Florida that he had been playing with down there. They were, I think, Junior Mance, because they were – him and Nat was in the army with Junior Mance. And Sam Jones was there. He’d been – they had been playing with Sam. So it was…

items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: And JimmyCobb on the drums and myself, rhythm section.

ctx.x: I was gigging round town then, you know. Been playing little gigs, small time dances uptown and them little club dates and stuff. So Cannon come to town and wanted me to play in the band. And I--they had Junior Mance on the piano. Phew. And that was an experience. And JimmyCobb on the drums and myself, rhythm section. But the band--it was alright. We travelled around and the band never got off the ground. You know what I mean. Never could make no money, you know.
You say with Junior that was--would you say that was really--
